statements.subject: sip
statements.description: Therefore, SIP should be used in conjunction with other protocols in order to provide complete services to the users.

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: Proxy, location, and registrar servers defined above are logical entities; implementations MAY combine them into a single application.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The start-line, each message-header line, and the empty line MUST be terminated by a carriage-return line-feed sequence (CRLF).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Note that the empty line MUST be present even if the message-body is not.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Request-URI MUST NOT contain unescaped spaces or control characters and MUST NOT be enclosed in "<>".

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: SIP elements MAY support Request-URIs with schemes other than "sip" and "sips", for example the "tel" URI scheme of RFC 2806 [9].

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: SIP elements MAY translate non-SIP URIs using any mechanism at their disposal, resulting in SIP URI, SIPS URI, or some other scheme.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: To be compliant with this specification, applications sending SIP messages MUST include a SIP-Version of "SIP/2.0".

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The SIP-Version string is case-insensitive, but implementations MUST send upper-case.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client is not required to examine or display the Reason-Phrase.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: implementations MAY choose other text, for example, in the language indicated in the Accept-Language header field of the request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: However, it is RECOMMENDED that header fields which are needed for proxy processing (Via, Route, Record-Route, Proxy-Require, Max-Forwards, and Proxy-Authorization, for example) appear towards the top of the message to facilitate rapid parsing.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Multiple header field rows with the same field-name MAY be present in a message if and only if the entire field-value for that header field is defined as a comma-separated list (that is, if follows the grammar defined in Section 7.3).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: It MUST be possible to combine the multiple header field rows into one "field-name: field-value" pair, without changing the semantics of the message, by appending each subsequent field-value to the first, each separated by a comma.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Multiple header field rows with these names MAY be present in a message, but since their grammar does not follow the general form listed in Section 7.3, they MUST NOT be combined into a single header field row.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Implementations MUST be able to process multiple header field rows with the same name in any combination of the single-value-per-line or comma-separated value forms.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Even though an arbitrary number of parameter pairs may be attached to a header field value, any given parameter-name MUST NOT appear more than once.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If a header field appears in a message not matching its category (such as a request header field in a response), it MUST be ignored.
actions: ignore mismatched header field

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A compact form MAY be substituted for the longer form of a header field name at any time without changing the semantics of the message.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A header field name MAY appear in both long and short forms within the same message.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Implementations MUST accept both the long and short forms of each header name.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Requests, including new requests defined in extensions to this specification, MAY contain message bodies unless otherwise noted.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: All responses MAY include a body.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Internet media type of the message body MUST be given by the Content-Type header field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the body has undergone any encoding such as compression, then this MUST be indicated by the Content-Encoding header field; otherwise, Content-Encoding MUST be omitted.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The "multipart" MIME type defined in RFC 2046 [11] MAY be used within the body of the message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Implementations that send requests containing multipart message bodies MUST send a session description as a non-multipart message body if the remote implementation requests this through an Accept header field that does not contain multipart.
actions: send session description as non-multipart message body

statements.subject: message
statements.description: SIP messages MAY contain binary bodies or body parts.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The "chunked" transfer encoding of HTTP/1.1 MUST NOT be used for SIP.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Implementations processing SIP messages over stream-oriented transports MUST ignore any CRLF appearing before the start-line [H4.1].
actions: ignore any CRLF bytes appearing before the start-line of the SIP message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A valid SIP request formulated by a UAC MUST, at a minimum, contain the following header fields: To, From, CSeq, Call-ID, Max-Forwards, and Via; all of these header fields are mandatory in all SIP requests.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The initial Request-URI of the message SHOULD be set to the value of the URI in the To field.
actions: Set initial Request-URI to the value of the URI in the To field

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: When a provider wishes to configure a UA with an outbound proxy, it is RECOMMENDED that this be done by providing it with a pre-existing route set with a single URI, that of the outbound proxy.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a pre-existing route set is present, the procedures for populating the Request-URI and Route header field detailed in Section 12.2.1.1 MUST be followed (even though there is no dialog), using the desired Request-URI as the remote target URI.
actions: Follow Section 12.2.1.1 procedures for populating Request-URI
Follow Section 12.2.1.1 procedures for populating Route header field
Use desired Request-URI as the remote target URI

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The To header field MAY contain a SIP or SIPS URI, but it may also make use of other URI schemes (the tel URL (RFC 2806 [9]), for example) when appropriate.

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: All SIP implementations MUST support the SIP URI scheme.

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: Any implementation that supports TLS MUST support the SIPS URI scheme.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A request outside of a dialog MUST NOT contain a To tag; the tag in the To field of a request identifies the peer of the dialog.
actions: omit To tag from outgoing request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A UAC SHOULD use the display name "Anonymous", along with a syntactically correct, but otherwise meaningless URI (like sip:thisis@anonymous.invalid), if the identity of the client is to remain hidden.
actions: Set From header display name to 'Anonymous'
Set From header URI to syntactically correct but meaningless URI

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The From field MUST contain a new "tag" parameter, chosen by the UAC.
actions: Generate new tag value chosen by the UAC
Include tag parameter in From header field

statements.subject: message
statements.description: It MUST be the same for all requests and responses sent by either UA in a dialog.
actions: set Call-ID header field equal to the Call-ID established for the dialog

statements.subject: message
statements.description: It SHOULD be the same in each registration from a UA.
actions: reuse same Call-ID header field value across registrations from the same UA

statements.subject: client
statements.description: the Call-ID header field MUST be selected by the UAC as a globally unique identifier over space and time unless overridden by method-specific behavior.
actions: select a globally unique Call-ID value for the new request

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: Use of cryptographically random identifiers (RFC 1750 [12]) in the generation of Call-IDs is RECOMMENDED.

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: Implementations MAY use the form "localid@host".

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The method MUST match that of the request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The sequence number value MUST be expressible as a 32-bit unsigned integer and MUST be less than 2**31.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As long as it follows the above guidelines, a client may use any mechanism it would like to select CSeq header field values.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A UAC MUST insert a Max-Forwards header field into each request it originates with a value that SHOULD be 70.
actions: Insert Max-Forwards header field into each originated request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the UAC creates a request, it MUST insert a Via into that request.
actions: insert Via header into outgoing request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The protocol name and protocol version in the header field MUST be SIP and 2.0, respectively.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The Via header field value MUST contain a branch parameter.
actions: include branch parameter in Via header field value

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The branch parameter value MUST be unique across space and time for all requests sent by the UA.
actions: generate globally unique branch parameter value for Via header

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The branch ID inserted by an element compliant with this specification MUST always begin with the characters "z9hG4bK".
actions: prefix branch ID value with the magic cookie 'z9hG4bK'

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Contact header field MUST be present and contain exactly one SIP or SIPS URI in any request that can result in the establishment of a dialog.
actions: Include Contact header field in outgoing dialog-establishing request
Ensure Contact header field contains exactly one SIP or SIPS URI

statements.subject: message
statements.description: That is, the Contact header field value contains the URI at which the UA would like to receive requests, and this URI MUST be valid even if used in subsequent requests outside of any dialogs.
actions: Populate Contact header URI with a globally valid address reachable outside any dialog context

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the Request-URI or top Route header field value contains a SIPS URI, the Contact header field MUST contain a SIPS URI as well.
actions: Set Contact header URI scheme to SIPS when Request-URI or top Route header contains a SIPS URI

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the UAC supports extensions to SIP that can be applied by the server to the response, the UAC SHOULD include a Supported header field in the request listing the option tags (Section 19.2) for those extensions.
actions: include Supported header field in request listing option tags for supported extensions

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The option tags listed MUST only refer to extensions defined in standards-track RFCs.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the UAC wishes to insist that a UAS understand an extension that the UAC will apply to the request in order to process the request, it MUST insert a Require header field into the request listing the option tag for that extension.
actions: insert Require header field into request listing option tag for required extension

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the UAC wishes to apply an extension to the request and insist that any proxies that are traversed understand that extension, it MUST insert a Proxy-Require header field into the request listing the option tag for that extension.
actions: insert Proxy-Require header field into request listing option tag for required extension

statements.subject: message
statements.description: As with the Supported header field, the option tags in the Require and Proxy-Require header fields MUST only refer to extensions defined in standards-track RFCs.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: SIP requests MAY contain a MIME-encoded message-body.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Unless there is local policy specifying otherwise, the destination MUST be determined by applying the DNS procedures described in [4] as follows.
actions: apply DNS procedures from [4] to determine destination

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the first element in the route set indicated a strict router (resulting in forming the request as described in Section 12.2.1.1), the procedures MUST be applied to the Request-URI of the request.
actions: apply DNS procedures to Request-URI

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Independent of which URI is used as input to the procedures of [4], if the Request-URI specifies a SIPS resource, the UAC MUST follow the procedures of [4] as if the input URI were a SIPS URI.
actions: apply DNS procedures as if input URI were SIPS URI

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: Local policy MAY specify an alternate set of destinations to attempt.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the Request-URI contains a SIPS URI, any alternate destinations MUST be contacted with TLS.
actions: contact alternate destinations using TLS

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: However, that approach for configuring an outbound proxy is NOT RECOMMENDED; a pre-existing route set with a single URI SHOULD be used instead.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the request contains a Route header field, the request SHOULD be sent to the locations derived from its topmost value, but MAY be sent to any server that the UA is certain will honor the Route and Request-URI policies specified in this document (as opposed to those in RFC 2543).
actions: send request to locations derived from topmost Route header field value

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In particular, a UAC configured with an outbound proxy SHOULD attempt to send the request to the location indicated in the first Route header field value instead of adopting the policy of sending all messages to the outbound proxy.
actions: send request to location indicated in first Route header field value

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The UAC SHOULD follow the procedures defined in [4] for stateful elements, trying each address until a server is contacted.
actions: follow DNS procedures for stateful elements
try each address in ordered set until a server is contacted
create new transaction for each address attempt

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a timeout error is received from the transaction layer, it MUST be treated as if a 408 (Request Timeout) status code has been received.
actions: treat timeout error as 408 Request Timeout response

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If a fatal transport error is reported by the transport layer (generally, due to fatal ICMP errors in UDP or connection failures in TCP), the condition MUST be treated as a 503 (Service Unavailable) status code.
actions: treat fatal transport error as 503 Service Unavailable response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A UAC MUST treat any final response it does not recognize as being equivalent to the x00 response code of that class, and MUST be able to process the x00 response code for all classes.
actions: treat_unrecognized_final_response_as_x00_class_equivalent

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A UAC MUST treat any provisional response different than 100 that it does not recognize as 183 (Session Progress).
actions: treat_unrecognized_provisional_response_as_183_Session_Progress

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A UAC MUST be able to process 100 and 183 responses.
actions: process_100_response
process_183_response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If more than one Via header field value is present in a response, the UAC SHOULD discard the message.
actions: discard response message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Upon receipt of a redirection response (for example, a 301 response status code), clients SHOULD use the URI(s) in the Contact header field to formulate one or more new requests based on the redirected request.
actions: formulate new requests using URIs from Contact header field

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As with proxy recursion, a client processing 3xx class responses MUST NOT add any given URI to the target set more than once.
actions: reject duplicate URI addition to target set

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the original request had a SIPS URI in the Request-URI, the client MAY choose to recurse to a non-SIPS URI, but SHOULD inform the user of the redirection to an insecure URI.
actions: recurse to non-SIPS URI

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As the target set grows, the client MAY generate new requests to the URIs in any order.
actions: generate new requests to URIs in target set in any order

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Requests to the URIs MAY be generated serially or in parallel.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Failures SHOULD be detected through failure response codes (codes greater than 399); for network errors the client transaction will report any transport layer failures to the transaction user.
actions: detect failure via response code greater than 399

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a failure for a particular contact address is received, the client SHOULD try the next contact address.
actions: try next contact address
create new client transaction to deliver new request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: a UAC MUST copy the entire URI from the target set into the Request-URI, except for the "method-param" and "header" URI parameters (see Section 19.1.1 for a definition of these parameters).
actions: copy entire URI from target set into Request-URI
exclude method-param and header URI parameters from copy

statements.subject: message
statements.description: As a general rule, if the header field can accept a comma-separated list of values, then the new header field value MAY be appended to any existing values in the original redirected request.
actions: append new header field value to existing values in original redirected request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the header field does not accept multiple values, the value in the original redirected request MAY be overwritten by the header field value communicated in the contact address.
actions: overwrite header field value with value communicated in contact address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It is RECOMMENDED that the UAC reuse the same To, From, and Call-ID used in the original redirected request, but the UAC MAY also choose to update the Call-ID header field value for new requests, for example.
actions: reuse To header from original redirected request
reuse From header from original redirected request
reuse Call-ID from original redirected request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Finally, once the new request has been constructed, it is sent using a new client transaction, and therefore MUST have a new branch ID in the top Via field as discussed in Section 8.1.1.7.
actions: assign new branch ID to top Via field of new request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In all other respects, requests sent upon receipt of a redirect response SHOULD re-use the header fields and bodies of the original request.
actions: re-use header fields and bodies from original request in new request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response is received, the UAC SHOULD follow the authorization procedures of Section 22.2 and Section 22.3 to retry the request with credentials.
actions: follow_authorization_procedures_section_22.2_22.3
retry_request_with_credentials

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If possible, the UAC SHOULD retry the request, either omitting the body or using one of a smaller length.
actions: retry_request_omitting_body_or_with_smaller_body

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The UAC SHOULD retry sending the request, this time only using content with types listed in the Accept header field in the response, with encodings listed in the Accept-Encoding header field in the response, and with languages listed in the Accept-Language in the response.
actions: retry_request_using_Accept_listed_content_types
retry_request_using_Accept-Encoding_listed_encodings
retry_request_using_Accept-Language_listed_languages

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD retry the request, this time, using a SIP URI.
actions: retry_request_with_SIP_URI

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The UAC SHOULD retry the request, this time omitting any extensions listed in the Unsupported header field in the response.
actions: retry_request_omitting_extensions_in_Unsupported_header

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This new request constitutes a new transaction and SHOULD have the same value of the Call-ID, To, and From of the previous request, but the CSeq should contain a new sequence number that is one higher than the previous.
statements.post_cond: new_transaction.Call-ID = prev_transaction.Call-ID & new_transaction.To = prev_transaction.To & new_transaction.From = prev_transaction.From & new_transaction.CSeq = prev_transaction.CSeq + 1
actions: create_new_transaction
set_Call-ID_equal_to_previous_request
set_To_equal_to_previous_request
set_From_equal_to_previous_request
set_CSeq_to_previous_CSeq_plus_one

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a request is accepted, all state changes associated with it MUST be performed.
actions: perform all state changes associated with the accepted request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it is rejected, all state changes MUST NOT be performed.
actions: rollback all state changes associated with the rejected request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: UASs SHOULD process the requests in the order of the steps that follow in this section (that is, starting with authentication, then inspecting the method, the header fields, and so on throughout the remainder of this section).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Once a request is authenticated (or authentication is skipped), the UAS MUST inspect the method of the request.
actions: inspect_request_method

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the UAS recognizes but does not support the method of a request, it MUST generate a 405 (Method Not Allowed) response.
actions: generate_405_response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The UAS MUST also add an Allow header field to the 405 (Method Not Allowed) response.
actions: add_Allow_header_to_405_response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Allow header field MUST list the set of methods supported by the UAS generating the message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a UAS does not understand a header field in a request (that is, the header field is not defined in this specification or in any supported extension), the server MUST ignore that header field and continue processing the message.
actions: ignore unknown header field
continue processing the message

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A UAS SHOULD ignore any malformed header fields that are not necessary for processing requests.
actions: ignore malformed header field

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A UAS MAY apply any policy it wishes to determine whether to accept requests when the To header field is not the identity of the UAS.
actions: apply local policy to determine whether to accept request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, it is RECOMMENDED that a UAS accept requests even if they do not recognize the URI scheme (for example, a tel: URI) in the To header field, or if the To header field does not address a known or current user of this UAS.
actions: accept request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If, on the other hand, the UAS decides to reject the request, it SHOULD generate a response with a 403 (Forbidden) status code and pass it to the server transaction for transmission.
actions: generate 403 Forbidden response
pass response to server transaction for transmission

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Request-URI uses a scheme not supported by the UAS, it SHOULD reject the request with a 416 (Unsupported URI Scheme) response.
actions: reject request with 416 Unsupported URI Scheme response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Request-URI does not identify an address that the UAS is willing to accept requests for, it SHOULD reject the request with a 404 (Not Found) response.
actions: reject request with 404 Not Found response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the request has no tag in the To header field, the UAS core MUST check the request against ongoing transactions.
actions: check request against ongoing transactions

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the From tag, Call-ID, and CSeq exactly match those associated with an ongoing transaction, but the request does not match that transaction (based on the matching rules in Section 17.2.3), the UAS core SHOULD generate a 482 (Loop Detected) response and pass it to the server transaction.
statements.pre_cond: request.From.tag = ongoing_transaction.From.tag & request.Call-ID = ongoing_transaction.Call-ID & request.CSeq = ongoing_transaction.CSeq & request.matches_transaction = false
actions: generate 482 (Loop Detected) response
pass response to server transaction

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a UAS does not understand an option-tag listed in a Require header field, it MUST respond by generating a response with status code 420 (Bad Extension).
actions: Generate response with status code 420 (Bad Extension)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The UAS MUST add an Unsupported header field, and list in it those options it does not understand amongst those in the Require header field of the request.
actions: Add Unsupported header field to 420 response
List in Unsupported header all option-tags from Require not understood by UAS

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Note that Require and Proxy-Require MUST NOT be used in a SIP CANCEL request, or in an ACK request sent for a non-2xx response.
actions: Omit Require header field from CANCEL request
Omit Proxy-Require header field from CANCEL request
Omit Require header field from ACK for non-2xx response
Omit Proxy-Require header field from ACK for non-2xx response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: These header fields MUST be ignored if they are present in these requests.
statements.pre_cond: (message.method = CANCEL | (message.method = ACK & message.correlated_response_code != 2xx)) & (message.Require.present = true | message.Proxy-Require.present = true)
actions: Ignore Require header field when present in CANCEL request
Ignore Proxy-Require header field when present in CANCEL request
Ignore Require header field when present in ACK for non-2xx response
Ignore Proxy-Require header field when present in ACK for non-2xx response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: An ACK request for a 2xx response MUST contain only those Require and Proxy-Require values that were present in the initial request.
actions: Include in ACK Require values only those present in the initial request
Include in ACK Proxy-Require values only those present in the initial request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there are any bodies whose type (indicated by the Content-Type), language (indicated by the Content-Language) or encoding (indicated by the Content-Encoding) are not understood, and that body part is not optional (as indicated by the Content-Disposition header field), the UAS MUST reject the request with a 415 (Unsupported Media Type) response.
statements.pre_cond: (body.type.understood = false | body.language.understood = false | body.encoding.understood = false) & body.optional = false
actions: reject request with 415 Unsupported Media Type response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The response MUST contain an Accept header field listing the types of all bodies it understands, in the event the request contained bodies of types not supported by the UAS.
actions: include Accept header field listing all understood body types in 415 response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the request contained content encodings not understood by the UAS, the response MUST contain an Accept-Encoding header field listing the encodings understood by the UAS.
actions: include Accept-Encoding header field listing understood encodings in 415 response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the request contained content with languages not understood by the UAS, the response MUST contain an Accept-Language header field indicating the languages understood by the UAS.
actions: include Accept-Language header field indicating understood languages in 415 response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A UAS that wishes to apply some extension when generating the response MUST NOT do so unless support for that extension is indicated in the Supported header field in the request.
actions: do not apply extension when generating response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the desired extension is not supported, the server SHOULD rely only on baseline SIP and any other extensions supported by the client.
actions: rely only on baseline SIP and extensions supported by client when generating response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In rare circumstances, where the server cannot process the request without the extension, the server MAY send a 421 (Extension Required) response.
actions: send 421 (Extension Required) response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The needed extension(s) MUST be included in a Require header field in the response.
actions: include needed extensions in Require header field of 421 response

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: This behavior is NOT RECOMMENDED, as it will generally break interoperability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Any extensions applied to a non-421 response MUST be listed in a Require header field included in the response.
actions: list all applied extensions in Require header field of response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Of course, the server MUST NOT apply extensions not listed in the Supported header field in the request.
actions: do not apply extensions not listed in Supported header field of request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Additional behaviors specific to the response code in question, which are not detailed in this section, may also be required.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: UASs SHOULD NOT issue a provisional response for a non-INVITE request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Rather, UASs SHOULD generate a final response to a non-INVITE request as soon as possible.
actions: generate final response as soon as possible

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a 100 (Trying) response is generated, any Timestamp header field present in the request MUST be copied into this 100 (Trying) response.
actions: copy Timestamp header field from request into 100 (Trying) response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there is a delay in generating the response, the UAS SHOULD add a delay value into the Timestamp value in the response.
actions: add delay value to Timestamp header in response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This value MUST contain the difference between the time of sending of the response and receipt of the request, measured in seconds.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The From field of the response MUST equal the From header field of the request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Call-ID header field of the response MUST equal the Call-ID header field of the request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The CSeq header field of the response MUST equal the CSeq field of the request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Via header field values in the response MUST equal the Via header field values in the request and MUST maintain the same ordering.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If a request contained a To tag in the request, the To header field in the response MUST equal that of the request.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: However, if the To header field in the request did not contain a tag, the URI in the To header field in the response MUST equal the URI in the To header field; additionally, the UAS MUST add a tag to the To header field in the response (with the exception of the 100 (Trying) response, in which a tag MAY be present).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The same tag MUST be used for all responses to that request, both final and provisional (again excepting the 100 (Trying)).
actions: reuse the same To tag established in the first response for every subsequent non-100 response to the same request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST NOT send provisional (1xx) responses.
actions: suppress_1xx_response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST NOT retransmit responses.
actions: discard_response_state
suppress_retransmission

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST ignore ACK requests.
actions: discard_ACK

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A stateless UAS MUST ignore CANCEL requests.

process_groups_serially_targets_within_group_in_parallel
